title: A Semester for the Tryouts
premise: Emrys Winterbourne, a seventeen-year-old baker's kid who channels everything he can't say into bread, has spent his whole life keeping his head down at Halcyon Prep—especially since the accident three years ago that took his best friend Theo's memories of their friendship. When a college essay prompt demands one honest answer, Emrys writes the truth about the night of the accident, and the draft leaks, forcing Theo to confront fragments he's been suppressing. As loyalty to Theo's family—who blame Emrys—collides with the truth that Emrys was the one who pulled Theo from the water, Emrys must choose between protecting the found family he's built in the bakery and reclaiming the friend who forgot him. In the end, Theo remembers on his own terms, and Emrys submits an essay about bread, grief, and choosing to be seen.
about_author: Noor Thackeray is a former line cook turned novelist who grew up above her family's corner bakery in coastal Maine. She writes stories about quiet kids with loud hearts, and still believes the best confessions happen over warm bread.

chapters.title: The Sourdough Confession
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At Winterbourne's Bakery before dawn, Emrys bakes his anxiety into loaves while dodging questions about college applications. His father's gentle probing about 'the essay' makes him flinch. Emotional beat: establish Emrys's coping ritual and his terror of being perceived.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the common app prompt: describe a moment that changed you. Emrys freezes—the honest answer involves Theo Ashford, the boy who drowned-adjacent accident erased. He writes a safe lie about learning to bake. Beat: the cost of invisibility made concrete.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Forgot Me
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Theo, now a lacrosse star with new friends, walks past Emrys's bakery without recognition—but pauses at the smell of cardamom bread, unsettled. Emrys watches through glass. Beat: longing sharpened by proximity; memory as a locked room.

chapters.title: What I Wrote at 2 A.M.
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Alone, Emrys finally writes the true essay: the cliff, the river, the night Theo fell and Emrys dove in after him—and how Theo's parents asked him to stay away during recovery. Beat: catharsis; the relief and danger of honesty.

chapters.title: Shared Folders Have Consequences
chapters.summary: POV alternating Emrys/Theo. Emrys accidentally shares the draft with his study group; classmate Priya forwards it. By Monday, the whole school knows Emrys saved Theo—and that the Ashfords pushed him away. Beat: exposure; panic blooming into something like freedom.

chapters.title: The Ashford House Rules
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo confronts his parents, who admit they kept Emrys away out of guilt—they'd blamed him for egging Theo toward the cliff. Theo begins having flashbacks triggered by the leaked essay. Beat: loyalty vs. truth fractures inside Theo's family.

chapters.title: Bread for an Apology
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The bakery becomes sanctuary: Priya, Ms. Okafor, and even estranged classmates gather there, forming an unlikely found family around Emrys's ovens. But Mr. Ashford arrives with lawyers' letters demanding retraction. Beat: warmth under siege; community as armor.

chapters.title: Cardamom, River Water
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A taste of Emrys's signature loaf cracks the dam: Theo remembers the cliff, the fall, Emrys's hands pulling him up. He storms the bakery mid-rush and says Emrys's name for the first time in three years. Beat: climax of memory; joy tangled with rage.

chapters.title: The Night We Don't Talk About
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Theo and Emrys finally tell each other the whole truth—including Emrys's guilt over daring Theo to climb. Theo's parents arrive mid-conversation; Theo chooses Emrys's account over theirs publicly. Beat: climax of conflict; truth wins but costs.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Weeks later: the Ashfords soften, Theo lingers at the bakery every morning, and Emrys submits a final essay about bread, grief, and being seen—not the leaked draft, but the self it made him. Beat: resolution; found family and chosen identity rise together like dough.
